filtering

Source: vignettes/filtering.Rmd
filtering.Rmd
library(dicr)

After the cleaning stage, we can pass records through an optional filtering stage.

To filter records, you must add a filter section to the source configuration YAML. The filter section uses the following schema:

filter:
  filtered_row_count: <integer>
  filters:
    - column: <column_name>
      predicate: eq|neq|gt|lt|gte|lte|in|contains|is_na
      value: <appropriately typed value, omitted for `is_na` predicate>
      negate: true|false <optional, default false>
      conjunction: <optional mapping to another filter rule>
        type: and|or|xor
        other:
          column: <other_column_name>
          predicate: <predicate, as above>
          negate: <boolean, as above>
          conjunction: <arbitrarily nested mapping>

The filtered_row_count value is a quality-assurance check to verify that the filters worked as intended. You should compute this manually before adding it to the config.

The filters identify filter rules that exclude rows that match the filters. In other words, to exclude deaths that occurred after 2025, you would use the following filter:

filter:
  ...
  filters:
    - column: death_year
      predicate: gt
      value: 2025

When multiple filter rules are provided, filter_source applies them sequentially, filtering out rows that match any of the filters.

For example, the following configuration would filter out deaths based on year and location:

filter:
  ...
  filters:
    - column: death_year
      predicate: gt
      value: 2025
    - column: death_location
      predicate: eq
      value: WORK RELEASE

Filter predicates

Filter rules can use the following predicates:

  • eq: Filters rows where column == value
  • neq: Filters row where column != value
  • gt: Filters rows where column > value
  • lt: Filters rows where column < value
  • gte: Filters rows where column >= value
  • lte: Filters rows where column <= value
  • in: Filters rows where column %in% value
  • contains: Filters rows where stringr::str_detect(column, value)
  • is_na: Filters rows where is.na(column)

Filter negation

Sometimes, it’s easier to filter rows by checking whether a condition is false rather than true. For example, if you wanted to filter deaths to only include a specific list of facilities, you would use the following rule:

filter:
  ...
  filters:
    - column: facility
      predicate: in
      negate: true
      value: ["Facility One", "Facility Two"]

This rule would filter any rows where the facility name does not match one of the listed values.

Conjunctions

In other cases, you may need to use more complex combinations of filters to get the desired result. For instance, imagine that Facility One was converted to a civil commitment center in July 2024, but it was used as a regular prison in earlier years. To filter out deaths that occured in Facility One after July 1, 2024, you can use the following rule:

filter:
  ...
  filters:
    - column: facility
      predicate: eq
      value: Facility One
      conjunction:
        type: and
        other:
          column: death_date
          predicate: gte
          value: 2024-07-01

There are three possible conjunction types:

  • and: Filters rows where the top-level condition and other are both true
  • or: Filters rows where the top-level condition or other are true. This is only useful for nested conjunctions, since top-level conditions are already applied additively. In other words, use it for checking that A & (B | C), not for A | (B & C).
  • xor: Filters rows where either the top-level condition or other are true, but not both.

Script-based filtering

Of course, as with extracting and cleaning data, it is sometimes easier to write a bespoke script to perform more complex operations. The filtering stage uses essentially the same contract for script-based processing as the other stages in the pipeline.

To use a filter script, replace the filters attribute with a script attribute that contains the path to the filter script (relative to the project root).

filter:
  filtered_row_count: 25
  script: path/to/filter/script.R'

The filter script must define a top-level function called filter_records that takes cleaned_records (the cleaned dataframe) and source_config as inputs and returns a list containing data (the filtered dataframe), filtered_records (a character vector with the record locators for each row removed during the filtering process), and warnings (a character vector of warning messages).
